title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 337
paragraphs: After this, they said, this same king descended alive into the place the Greeks call Hades, and there played at dice with Demeter. In some throws he beat her, and in others she beat him; and he came back again bringing as a gift from her a handkerchief of gold. Because of Rhampsinitos's descent, they told me, the Egyptians after his return held a festival, which I know from my own observation they still keep even in my own time; but whether they hold the feast for this reason or for some other, I cannot say. In any case, on the very day of the festival the priests weave a complete robe, and then they bind up the eyes of one of them with a headband, and leading him in the robe to the path that goes to the temple of Demeter, they depart, going back by themselves. This priest, they say, with his eyes bound, is led by two wolves to the temple of Demeter, which lies twenty furlongs from the city, and then the wolves lead him back again from the temple to the same spot.
